title: Weekly Regional Review
author: Andy · Hortonville Polar Bears Statistician
overview: De Pere beat us 3-2 Saturday. First loss since October 26, 2024. Sucks, but we’ll survive and now know what to expect against De Pere when we see them again in the sectional.  It should be said that with a full game of Rome in, it’s possible Hortonville scores another goal.  The positive is the team is deep enough to go unbeaten against solid competition without him. Last week, we handled Fond du Lac 4-1 on the road and Green Bay Preble 3-1 at De Pere, all without him.

De Pere's seeding probably jumps ahead of ours now.  Appleton North's still unbeaten in conference and at 7-1-2 overall.  Tuesday we find out if they’re for real.  On film, they’ve looked much better than I originally gave them credit for. Neenah dropped one to Oshkosh West on the 15th, not a disaster, Oshkosh West's a solid team, but that's not what a top team does in the middle of September.

Kimberly continues to spiral this season. 2-6-3 after playing Bay Port to a scoreless draw. Hard to circle that game anymore.  Except that if the boys do what they should, Hortonville gets its first ever win against them.  So we have that going for us, which is nice.

Hudson lost 0-1 to Hill-Murray (a top MN team), so scratch another team from the ranks of undefeated D1 teams. I believe that leaves it at 3 (Arrowhead, Middleton, and DeForest).  And DeForest Area's sitting at 10-0.  Impressive coming up from the D2 championship game last season.

•  Appleton North, Tuesday: big conference and seeding game. They're unbeaten in conference and averaging better than 3 goals a game, but they still haven't played anybody yet.  It’s a home game and we’ll have to show up and show out.
•  Appleton West, Thursday: 0-7-1, 32 goals allowed against 4 scored. This one should not be close. Hopefully some continued confidence and a chance to play the bench.
•  Roman's minutes: out since the Neenah tie on the 1st, back for limited minutes against De Pere. This week will be a big step to get him back into full playing shape.

games.review: The one that actually decides something. North is unbeaten in conference, but nobody on their schedule is us or Neenah yet. Huge game to recover from the DP match.
Neenah's chance to answer the Oshkosh West stumble. Appleton East has quietly played very solid ball.

Eau Claire Memorial just put seven on River Falls, their best result of the year. Hudson just lost 0-1 to Hill-Murray, their first loss of the season, so this is their response game.  This is the Big Rivers derby.  But ECM is kind of the Kimberly of the conference this season.  So I’m not assuming they’ll put up the fight I would hope.
Two of the stronger Division 1 teams in the state. Worth a glance if you care about who's actually good outside our pocket of Wisconsin.
West is 0-7-1 and has been outscored 32-4 on the season. This should be a breather game for us. But I shouldn’t be that overconfident.  Still have to go out and play the game.

games.matchup: Green Bay Preble at Notre Dame Academy
games.review: Preble's coming off a bounce-back win at D.C. Everest after losing to us. Notre Dame Academy is probably the best team in D3.
SPASH just got run over 4-0 at home by Appleton East. Hudson just took their first loss of the year. Somebody's week is about to get worse.

title: Weekly Regional Review
author: Andy · Hortonville Polar Bears Statistician
overview: We had, arguably, the best week of any team in the FVA. A 2-1 win over Appleton East, then a 6-0 beatdown of Bay Port.  All without Rome.  Not too shabby.

FVA at this point is us and Neenah at the top, with Appleton North a question mark. Neenah's win over Hamilton is a real result, not conference padding. Appleton North allowed one goal all week, which is legitimately good, but their schedule was Kaukauna, West De Pere, and a draw with Preble.  The Preble result was interesting. But none of that is against  Neenah or us. Until they actually play one of the top teams in conference, I can’t put any stock in them.

Kimberly's having a down year (sorry Cooper), and the results back it up. Beating Fond du Lac in conference play is fine, but getting outscored 8-1 combined by Hudson and Stillwater in the same weekend is not a fluke. That's not the Kimberly we're used to seeing on the schedule.

We have a huge week.  Really have to make sure we don’t lose focus on Fond du Lac with Preble and De Pere looming.  We make it through this week and we’re in a really good spot heading into the back half of the season.

•  Preble on Thursday: harder than the record suggests. Their draw with Appleton North and solid loss to De Pere make it look, on paper, like we should beat them solidly.  But they’ve always been pesky to us.
•  De Pere on Saturday: a coin flip game. They’re hot, beating Preble 3-0 and Bay Port 5-0 in the same week.
•  The schedule itself: three games in five days. By Saturday, legs might decide more than tactics do.

One more thing worth saying out loud: Hudson is legit. A 4-0 shutout of Kimberly means a lot more than the 8-0 they put on Menomonie.  They’re a top 5 team.  Unless something goes crazy, the sectional final will go through Hudson.

games.review: First game of our gauntlet. Fond du Lac just answered a loss to Kimberly with a good road win over Manitowoc Lincoln, so this isn't the free opener the schedule makes it look like.

Proving point for North. Kimberly's trying to answer back-to-back losses to Hudson and Stillwater that exposed a real gap against good competition.  If North wins, it’s their first win against a decent FVA team – in my opinion.
This one will be interesting.  Preble is physical and aggressive.  But if they get down, they lose it a bit.  We should win, but need to really show up.
Hopefully Everest can give DP a game and give them some tired legs heading into our match up on Saturday.  It will be checking out the result of this one.

games.matchup: Green Bay Preble vs. D.C. Everest
games.review: Preble sandwiched between facing us Thursday and this one two days later. Worth watching how much the midweek game takes out of them.
Closes our three-game gauntlet. This is a big game, regardless of how the rest of the week goes.  And if we’re super lucky, the last big game before we get Roman back.

Neenah's probably the second-best team in this conference right now behind us, and a good week here keeps that gap from closing.  They should be able to beat Rapids pretty handily, but it could be a trap game for Neenah.  And Neenah has always been my FVA Tottenham.  Growing up in a Neenah/Menasha rivalry, I dislike Neenah immensely.
